svg.title: Non-contact water rescue from secure land — person still in water
svg.desc: Working non-contact water-rescue card from secure land. Call Triple Zero, remain on secure land, and try Talk, then a safe Reach with a long aid, then Throw a rope or buoyant object. Stop if the rescuer could fall or be pulled in, and never put a rope around the rescuer. If already on a craft, stay aboard and use its rescue equipment and procedures only within current training; no craft-handling method is provided. Water entry, swimming, towing, in-water resuscitation and contact rescue are excluded. Once the person is on a safe firm surface, use Card 2.
svg.text: DROWNING / WATER RESCUE — CARD 1
Person still in water — non-contact help from secure land
WARNING — AQUATIC-RESCUE REVIEW OUTSTANDING
Subjective estimates: source match 95%; decision layout 60%.
Not probabilities of safe rescue, treatment success or survival.
This card does not qualify you to enter water or make contact.
Follow 000. Never enter because this picture shows a rescue.
Independent aquatic-rescue and practical review remains open.
Stressed-reader review remains open.
1 — SHOUT FOR HELP — CALL 000
Name a helper to call. If alone, use speaker if available.
Keep the person in sight. Tell 000 the location.
Say whether the person responds.
No contact? Use Chapter 3's satellite, radio or PLB emergency path.
2 — STAY ON SECURE LAND
Can you help without entering, falling or being pulled in?
YES — try TALK. Then REACH or THROW only
while you and the aid stay secure.
NO / UNSURE — stay back and update 000.
Guide trained rescuers. Do not enter.
Do not enter because a first attempt failed.
ALREADY ON A CRAFT?
Stay aboard. Use its rescue equipment and procedures only within
your current training, and follow 000. This card gives no craft method.
3 — TALK — SAFEST FIRST
Call to the person. Reassure them.
Tell them to hold any float and move toward the nearest safe edge,
if able. Keep pointing to safety. Do not enter the water.
4 — REACH — ONLY FROM A STABLE POSITION
Use a long, sturdy reach aid. Stay low and behind the edge.
Tell the person to hold it. Pull only while the bank, aid,
grip and your balance remain secure.
Could you be pulled in? STOP.
Do not turn a reach into a water entry.
5 — THROW — AID WITHOUT ENTRY
Throw a rope or something that floats within reach:
lifejacket, lifebuoy, bodyboard, inflated ball or buoyant cooler lid.
Tell them to hold it and keep their face clear.
Try again from land if the first throw misses.
Bring them toward a safe exit only while you remain secure.
Cannot grasp or follow? Keep them in sight and update 000.

g.text: Throw from land; no rope around the rescuer.

svg.text: STOP BOUNDARY
No wading, swimming, towing, in-water breaths or contact rescue
is taught here. Use a higher-risk method only if you already have
current aquatic-rescue training, suitable flotation and conditions
within that training. Chest compressions are ineffective in water
and must not be attempted there.
ON SAFE, FIRM SURFACE → USE CARD 2
WORKING DRAFT • CARD 1 OF 2 • secure-land path only • follow 000
